nodes.title: Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your picture)

promptState.text: Relight this photograph as a clear winter night, two hours after sunset. The overcast sky turns deep navy blue with many small stars, the fir trees and the bare birches fall into dark blue shadow with soft moonlight on their snow, and the snow on the ground and on the roof turns soft moonlit blue. All four windows glow warm yellow from inside, with the curtains lit from behind. The iron lantern to the right of the green door and the small lamp to its left are lit, and throw a warm pool of orange light over the door, its wreath, the porch and the log wall. The warm light from the lower windows and the porch falls in soft patches across the snow in front of the cottage and along the stone path, fading into blue further from the house. A thin line of pale smoke rises from the brick chimney into the dark sky. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the log walls, the thatched roof and its thick snow, the icicles, the wooden porch, the green door and its wreath, the brick chimney, the snowy bushes, the trees, the stone path, the camera angle and the framing.

MODELS AND NODES USED IN THIS WORKFLOW

 P-H3 Image needs ComfyUI 0.44.0 or newer, the first version with these nodes. On an older ComfyUI the nodes show red: update ComfyUI first.

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors19.5 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models/h3

Create the h3 folder if it does not exist. This is the First and Last Frame version of MiniMax H3 (fl2va): if you did Episode 41 you may already have it.

 LoRA (in LoRA Loader Pixaroma)

Download p-h3-image_lora_bf16.safetensors1.82 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/loras/h3

Create the h3 folder inside loras if it does not exist.

 Load CLIP

Download p-h3-image_text_encoder_int8_convrot.safetensors4.77 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/text_encoders

 Load VAE

Download p-h3-image_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors2.93 GB  

Place in: ComfyUI/models/vae

P-H3 Image is built on MiniMax H3, so the MiniMax H3 Community License applies. Read it and check what it says for your country before you use the model.

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Give the model one picture and change the time of day. The demo takes a snowy cottage from a grey winter day to a clear night, with the windows and the lantern lit.

 Steps

  1. Load your picture in Load Image Mini Pixaroma.
  2. Write the new light in Prompt Pixaroma.
  3. Click a size on Number Pick Pixaroma if you want a smaller or bigger result.
  4. Leave the seed on F to repeat a result, or switch it to R to try a new one every Run.
  5. Press Run. Drag across Image Compare Pixaroma to see before and after.

 Writing the prompt

  1. Say the new time of day: Relight this photograph as a clear winter night, two hours after sunset.
  2. Say what happens to the sky and to everything far away: The overcast sky turns deep navy blue with many small stars.
  3. Name each light that comes on and what it falls on: The iron lantern to the right of the green door ... throw a warm pool of orange light over the door.
  4. Say where the light reaches on the ground and where it ends: across the snow in front of the cottage ... fading into blue further from the house.
  5. End with what to keep, and name each thing. Always add the camera angle and the framing.

 Good to know

  • The picture stays in place. On all 4 seeds and at all 4 sizes the cottage stayed exactly where it was, so the before and after line up.
  • Try a few seeds. All 4 came out well, but the smoke was different on each one, and on seed 3 it came out orange.
  • Not every light comes on. The prompt asks for both lamps beside the door, but at 4 megapixels the small one on the left lit only on seed 3.
  • A new size gives a new picture. With the same seed, the small lamp lit at 2 megapixels and stayed off at 1, 4 and 8. Find your size first, then try seeds.
  • Warm light changes colours. Near the lantern the green door turns olive and the red wreath turns gold.
  • Night held the frame, blue hour did not. On a picture of a shop, a clear night kept the shop in place, but asking for the blue hour moved the camera on all 4 seeds.
  • You can ask for a small change at the same time. On that shop, a bicycle came out cleanly on all 4 seeds while the day turned to night.
  • The result has the shape of your picture. The demo goes in at 2048 x 2048 and comes out the same size.
  • There is no prompt upsampler here. With a detailed prompt like this one it made no clear difference in our tests, and it needs one more big download.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 fl2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. The LoRA in the next node turns it into P-H3 Image, a picture model. If you did Episode 41 you may already have this file.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (P-H3 Image) - The P-H3 Image LoRA from Pruna. Keep it on at strength 1: without it H3 is a video model and the picture falls apart.
  • Load CLIP (P-H3 Image text encoder) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the model understands. The type must be minimax.
  • Load VAE (P-H3 Image VAE) - Turns the finished render into the picture. It is made for P-H3 Image, a different file from the H3 video VAE.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your picture) - The picture to relight. Click it to upload your own, or pick one from the list.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (2. the new light) - Say the new time of day, name each light that comes on and what it falls on, then what to keep (see How to Use).
  • Number Pick Pixaroma (3. megapixels) - How big the result is. Click 1, 2, 4 (the demo) or 8 megapixels. A square picture comes out at 1024, 1440, 2048 or 2912 pixels on each side. A smaller size is faster.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. fixed or random) - The seed. F (fixed) repeats the result, R (random) tries a new one every Run. The demo uses seed 2.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (1 / 1 for pictures) - The noise schedule. P-H3 Image needs 1 and 1. Leave it as it is.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels (scales your picture) - Scales your picture to the size you clicked on Number Pick Pixaroma. The result comes out the same size and shape.
  • PH3 Image Conditioning (prompt + your picture) - Joins the prompt and your picture. With width and height on 0, the result takes the size and shape of the picture.
  • Basic Guider (no CFG) - Hands the model and the prompt to the sampler. P-H3 Image needs no CFG and no negative prompt.
  • KSampler Select (sampler) - The sampler. euler is the one in Pruna's own workflow. ComfyUI's template uses er_sde: the same speed, but it broke small words on a label in our tests.
  • Manual Sigmas (the 8 steps) - The 8 steps the model was trained on. More steps do not help, so leave these numbers as they are.
  • Random Noise - The starting noise, from the seed.
  • Sampler Custom Advanced (the render) - The render itself: 8 steps. The normal KSampler cannot take this hand-made step list, so this node does the job.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves the result) - Saves each result as PNG into ComfyUI/output/P-H3 Image Relight and shows it on the node.
  • Image Compare Pixaroma (before and after, drag across it) - Your picture and the result on top of each other. Drag across it to see the day turn into night.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: a smaller picture is much faster.

SizeTime
1 megapixelabout 8 s
2 megapixelsabout 12 s
4 megapixels (the demo)15 to 29 s
8 megapixelsabout 44 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3, and 10 GB for the LoRA, the text encoder and the VAE), so it takes longer. After that they stay in memory, if your PC has enough of it. Two testers with 16 GB cards: with 64 GB of RAM the next Runs were close to the times above; with 32 GB the models loaded from disk again on every Run, and each Run took about 4 times as long.

 On a smaller card

Click 1 or 2 on Number Pick Pixaroma. They look good too.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
